sources.title: Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana: The Autobiography of Kwame Nkrumah (1957)

leadership_drive.rationale: Founded the Convention People's Party and led Ghana to become the first sub-Saharan African colony to achieve independence (1957), then served as its first prime minister and president, extensively documented via the well-established political history of the period.

proactive_agency.rationale: Self-initiated the 'Positive Action' campaign of strikes and civil disobedience against colonial rule in 1950, resulting in his own imprisonment, a documented instance of unprompted direct political action.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Was imprisoned by British colonial authorities for organizing the 1950 Positive Action campaign, continuing his political organizing from prison — a specific, well-documented instance of continuing under real personal cost.

impact_motivation.rationale: Explicitly and consistently framed his political work around pan-African unity and decolonization rather than personal power alone, documented via his own extensive published writing (Africa Must Unite) and his sustained advocacy for the Organisation of African Unity.

persistence.rationale: Continued organizing for independence across multiple setbacks including imprisonment, documented via the well-established sequence of his political career from the 1940s through 1957.

persuasiveness.rationale: Built the Convention People's Party into a mass political movement capable of winning a decisive electoral mandate while he was still imprisoned in 1951, a specific, well-documented demonstration of organizing/persuasive capacity.

achievement_drive.rationale: Continued pursuing an ambitious pan-African political project (the Organisation of African Unity, industrialization projects) well beyond Ghana's own independence, evidencing sustained ambition beyond the initial achievement.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained direct political confrontation with British colonial authorities across a multi-year independence campaign, documented via the well-established record of his organizing and its consequences.

systems_abstraction.rationale: Developed a systematic pan-Africanist political framework linking individual national independence movements to a broader continental unification project, documented via his own extensive published political theory.

autonomy_need.rationale: Broke from more gradualist Gold Coast political figures to found his own more radical, independence-focused party, documented via the well-established split within Gold Coast nationalist politics.

planning_orientation.rationale: The Positive Action campaign's organized structure and the subsequent transition-to-independence process evidence real advance political planning.

discipline.rationale: Sustained a demanding organizing and later governing career across roughly two decades, evidenced by the scale of political and economic projects documented under his leadership.

social_assertiveness.rationale: Sustained a prominent international public political role, including extensive travel and speaking advocating pan-Africanism, documented via the well-established record of his international engagements.

adaptability.rationale: Moved between grassroots organizing, formal electoral politics, and international diplomacy across his career, suggesting real flexibility in political approach.

collaboration.rationale: Worked with a broad coalition of Gold Coast political organizers to build the Convention People's Party into a mass movement, suggesting real capacity for coalition-building despite his own strong personal leadership style.

mastery_orientation.rationale: Continued developing his political and organizational capability from early grassroots organizing through to national and international statesmanship.

decisiveness.rationale: Committed decisively to the Positive Action civil-disobedience strategy at a specific chosen moment rather than prolonged gradualist negotiation, documented via the well-established timing of that 1950 campaign.

independent_thinking.rationale: Advocated for immediate, complete independence and pan-African political union at a time when many contemporaries favored more gradual, incremental approaches, documented via his own explicit published political positions.

creative_originality.rationale: Developed and articulated a systematic pan-Africanist political philosophy that was genuinely novel in its scope and ambition for the period, documented via his own extensive published political theory.

deep_focus.rationale: Sustained organizing and later governing work required extended concentrated engagement with complex political and economic development projects.

curiosity.rationale: His extensive engagement with pan-African political theory and international diplomacy suggests real intellectual range beyond Ghana's own domestic politics.

provenance.notes: Third-batch diversity pick: 20th_century, sub_saharan_africa, politics/decolonization domain — a distinct trait shape and historical moment from the existing sub_saharan_africa roster (Mandela, Wangari Maathai, Chinua Achebe, Fela Kuti, Wole Soyinka), specifically the first-wave decolonization/pan-Africanist leadership era. Later authoritarian turn in his own presidency (post-1960, culminating in the 1966 coup that removed him) was reviewed and NOT scored as a personality trait per this project's own rule against reading outcomes backward into traits without direct behavioral evidence — the scored attributes here are grounded in the well-documented independence-era organizing period specifically.

holdReason: Confidence ceiling after two remediation rounds (genuine evidence additions targeting missing high-baseWeight attributes, then a rubric-floor correction bringing every row already tagged evidenceType "documented" up to scoring-rubric-v1's own 0.65 floor for that tier -- never touching strong_inference/inference rows, never adding fabricated evidence): avgConf 0.503 vs 0.55 floor.
